heard: Somewhere in your brain there may be a recording of your first birthday. So why can't you press play?

Remember being two? Four in ten people say they do. But those memories are probably rebuilt from photos and family stories.

So, can babies even make memories? Psychologist Caroline Rový Kolje tied the ribbon from a baby's ankle to a mobile. Three -month -olds learned that kicking made it dense and remembered it a week later.
In 2025, a Yale teen scanned awake babies. From about their first birthday, the hippocampus, the brain's memory, was already feeling away what they saw.
So the recorder works, it's the playback that fails.
One suspect comes from baby mice. In a lab in Toronto, young brains grow new neurons so fast they keep rewiring. Like renovating a library, while you're still shelving the books,
Then, months later, the team shone light on the cells that once held a lost memory, and it flickered back. Not deleted, just lost.
Words may be another lock. In New Zealand toddlers never describe the toy using words they learned afterwards.
It's mostly mice and small studies, so no one can promise your baby memories survive.
But they might still be in there. Feel the way before you had the words to find them. You were there. You just can't find the door.
